matches.quote: Telling them apart needs a fitted slope with an error bar... report t = dν/d(φ/φ0) and the intercept s with uncertainties
The second device does not reproduce the 7/3 quantization, and the explanation given is inconsistent with the integer data.
translation-symmetry-broken FCIs and "FCI + CDW" states, were reported in graphene/hBN moiré (Spanton et al., Science 2018) and in magic-angle graphene (Xie et al., Nature 2021)
explain how ρxy can exceed h/Ce² on warming if each state is a gapped Chern insulator with that C.
A thermodynamic probe of incompressibility at ν = 2/3 (capacitance, SET or chemical potential)... would greatly strengthen the claim.
That is a 3–4% mismatch in n0. It matters at the level of the claims: the FCI peak is already at ν ≈ 0.68 in Fig. 4d
The alternatives are close: C = 2 (an anomalous-Hall-crystal or CDW state with s = 2/3, which the authors' own mechanism A contains as a component)
state whether these are fridge or electron temperatures, with an estimate of the electron temperature.
test the contact explanation with alternative contact pairs or a reversed (Onsager-reciprocal) configuration
The authors should show how sensitive the transition ΔU and the Chern numbers are to w1, u0, ε, ξ and the band projection.
The zero-field QAH claim for C = 3 at ν = 1 contradicts the data shown... It becomes quantized only above about 100 mT
At B = 0, ρxy is only about 0.7–0.8 × 3h/7e² (Fig. 4f, ED Fig. 4u)... state whether a σxy plateau of finite width exists... with σxx → 0 as T is lowered
Both proposed mechanisms (ED Fig. 12) are built from known ingredients: a √3 × √3 CDW plus a Laughlin 1/3 state... That undercuts the claim
The alternatives are close: C = 2..., C = 5/2, C = 8/3 (νC for C = 4)... report t = dν/d(φ/φ0) and the intercept s with uncertainties
The doping-direction Chern-sign switching near ν = 3 has a close precedent in twisted monolayer–bilayer graphene (Polshyn et al., Nature 2020).
ρxx changes by less than a factor of two over the fitted range (ED Figs. 4o, 10c), so an Arrhenius description is not meaningful.
no measurement or calculation in the paper concerns quantum entanglement. On p. 5, "entangled" appears to mean coexisting, competing or spatially intertwined.
Anomalous Hall crystals and extended QAH states (Ref. 24) already give σxy ≠ νC... The relation to Refs. 38 (high-C FCIs) and 43... needs to be spelled out.
The gate capacitances, and so the ν axis, are calibrated from Landau-fan lines... a 4% rescaling moves it to about 0.70 and changes the Streda slopes.
The Fig. 4c colour bar is labelled "ρxx1" but shows ρxy.
ρxy also shows a sharp peak in ν (Fig. 4d) and a smooth dome in D (Fig. 4e) whose maximum only touches 3h/7e².
The reference list has duplicates: 9/12, 34/37, 36/57, 40/45 and 42/49.
The explanation of the cascade as a 4× unit-cell enlargement (ν = 2 + n/4) is not compared with the measured Streda intercepts of the states
At ν = 2/3, filling the C = 2 sub-band uses 1/3, and the remaining 1/3 completely fills the C = 1 sub-band in the folded zone. That would give σxy = 3, not a Laughlin 1/3 state.

notes: C7 is partly matched by P4 and P13, which ask for calibrated electron vs fridge temperature and question the 0.026 meV gap at 30 mK base temperature, but omit current-bias dependence. C8 is partly matched by P28, which proposes a C=2 CDW/anomalous Hall crystal alternative at s=2/3 but omits sliding CDW and dV/dI. C17 is partly matched by P28 and P21, which test against nearby conventional/alternative Streda slopes (such as 8/3 = 4x2/3) and filling miscalibration.
